title: perf-bench-scratch-kate-sullivan-llama13b-latency-throughput-2026-03-04
content:
Goal:
- Quick micro-bench to compare latency/throughput tradeoffs for Llama-2-13B (8k) under different batching + KV cache configs on a single A100-80GB host. Not a formal sweep, just notes for follow-up runs.

Setup:
- Model variant: Llama-2-13B-8k, converted and 4-bit quantized (GPTQ-like).
- Host: A100-80GB (single), CUDA 12.1, Triton disabled (we're using runtime v1.9 local runner).
- Runtime flags: transient_kv_cache=true, continuous_batching=true.
- Client: perf-runner v0.9.1 (python), synthetic prompt generator; text-only workloads.
- Measurement: 95th and 99th percentile latency of first token, and steady-state tokens/sec at given concurrency. Each measurement is average of 3 runs (2 min each).

Workloads:
- short: prompt_len=16 tokens, gen_len=32 tokens (reason: many interactive completions)
- medium: prompt_len=128, gen_len=128
- long: prompt_len=512, gen_len=512 (stress KV, attention memory)

Configs tested (quick):
A) Batch size 1 (no batching), KV cache warm
B) Batch size 8, continuous batching enabled, KV cache warm
C) Batch size 16, continuous batching enabled, KV cache warm
D) Batch size 8, KV cache cold (first requests)
E) Batch size 8 + prefix caching (reuse common prompt prefix)

Results (summary table, rough):
- Short workload (prompt16/gen32):
  A) p95=42ms, p99=62ms, tokens/sec(single)=260
  B) p95=55ms, p99=90ms, tokens/sec=980
  C) p95=80ms, p99=130ms, tokens/sec=1600
  D) p95=120ms, p99=220ms, tokens/sec=540 (cold kv hit)
  E) p95=38ms, p99=58ms, tokens/sec=1100 (prefix reuse helps latency + throughput)

- Medium workload (prompt128/gen128):
  A) p95=120ms, p99=190ms, tokens/sec=220
  B) p95=170ms, p99=260ms, tokens/sec=840
  C) p95=270ms, p99=420ms, tokens/sec=1400
  D) p95=360ms, p99=620ms, tokens/sec=480
  E) p95=115ms, p99=180ms, tokens/sec=900

- Long workload (prompt512/gen512):
  A) p95=480ms, p99=760ms, tokens/sec=160
  B) p95=650ms, p99=980ms, tokens/sec=640
  C) p95=1100ms, p99=1700ms, tokens/sec=1100
  D) p95=1500ms, p99=2400ms, tokens/sec=360
  E) p95=420ms, p99=700ms, tokens/sec=700

Observations / quick takeaways:
- Batching increases throughput substantially (up to ~6x) at the expense of tail latency. For interactive short prompts, batch=8 seems a reasonable sweet spot if some added p99 is acceptable.
- Cold KV cache (D) kills both latency and throughput — first requests pay heavy overhead. Warm cache or pre-warming is important for steady-state performance.
- Prefix caching (E) is surprisingly strong: for workloads with repeated prefixes, latency can be lower than single-request baseline because it avoids recomputing large prefix attention. Worth surfacing in recommendations.
- For long sequences, memory/attention cost increases nonlinearly; p99 jumps a lot with batch size 16 (C). Need to cap batching for long-seq workloads or fall back to streaming / chunking.
- Quantization (4-bit) looks OK for throughput but we need quality evals. No subjective degrade observed in short tests, but run formal eval later.

Notes on measurement noise and caveats:
- These runs are on single host; network overhead is minimal. Hosted environment will add variability.
- perf-runner uses synthetic prompts; real user distributions will alter distribution (more short chats).
- p99 here is single-token generation p99 (time to first token after request). End-to-end completion p99 is ~additive based on gen length — include in follow-ups.
- GPU power throttling observed on one run (temp spike) — ignore that run; will re-run stability sweep.

Quick actions / next runs:
- Re-run medium and long configs with batch-size auto-threshold (cap by seq length) to see improvement in p99.
- Add network-latency emulation (50ms) to simulate hosted edge.
- Run with Triton enabled + kernels v2 to compare both latency and throughput on same hardware.
- Run quality eval (BLEU/ROUGE or prompt-specific metrics) comparing fp16 vs 4-bit quant. Link to eval harness: github PR above.
- Add a simple pre-warm script to populate KV cache for common prefixes and measure warmup time and throughput ramp.

Quick ASCII chart (tokens/sec vs batch for short workload, avg of 3 runs):
- batch 1 : ||| 260 tps
- batch 8 : ||||||||||| 980 tps
- batch 16: |||||||||||||||||| 1600 tps
(visual: throughput scales sublinearly, doubling batch from 8->16 gives ~1.6x)

Questions to resolve:
- What's product decision for default batching window vs latency-sensitive routes? Per-route config or auto-throttle?
- Should we expose prefix-caching controls to customers or do it transparently? Security/segmentation concerns for shared prefixes across tenants.

Short-term hypothesis: default batch window=20ms + max_batch=8 yields good balance for chat-like short prompts; fallback to batch=1 if request marked low-latency. Need A/B on real traffic.

Notes to self: save these raw logs -> S3 path: s3://perf-logs/kate/2026-03-04/ (have csv + perf-runner JSON). Also create a dashboard tile in console perf -> p99 vs concurrency for Llama-13B.

End of scratch notes.
